title: Evolent Clinical Guideline 1764 for Knee Arthroscopy

criteria.text: There is clinical correlation of the individual's subjective complaints with objective exam findings and/or imaging (when applicable)
criteria.question: Do the objective exam findings and/or imaging correlate with the individual's reported complaints?

criteria.text: Knee pain with documented loss of function: Deviation from normal knee function which may include painful weight bearing and/or inadequate range of motion (> 10 degrees flexion contracture or < 110 degrees flexion or both) to accomplish age-appropriate activities of daily living (ADLs), occupational or athletic requirements)
criteria.question: Is knee pain documented together with a loss of function (for example painful weight bearing, a flexion contracture over 10 degrees or flexion under 110 degrees, or inability to do age-appropriate daily, occupational or athletic activities)?

criteria.text: Individual is medically stable and optimized for surgery
criteria.question: Is the individual documented as medically stable and optimized for surgery?

criteria.text: any treatable comorbidities are adequately medically managed such as diabetes, nicotine addiction, or an excessively high BMI
criteria.question: Are treatable comorbidities (for example diabetes, nicotine addiction, excessively high BMI) documented as adequately managed?

criteria.text: There should also be a shared decision between the patient and physician to proceed with knee surgery when comorbidities exist as it pertains to the increased risk of complications
criteria.question: Where comorbidities exist, is a shared decision between patient and physician to proceed with surgery despite the increased risk of complications documented?

criteria.text: comorbidities exist
criteria.question: Does the individual have comorbidities (for example diabetes, nicotine addiction, high BMI) that increase surgical risk?

criteria.text: Individual does not have an active local or systemic infection
criteria.question: Is the individual free of any active local or systemic infection?

criteria.text: Individual does not have active, untreated drug dependency (including but not limited to narcotics, opioids, or muscle relaxants)
criteria.question: Is the individual free of active, untreated drug dependency (narcotics, opioids, muscle relaxants or similar)?

criteria.text: engaged in a treatment program
criteria.question: If drug dependency is present, is the individual engaged in a treatment program?

criteria.text: No intra-articular cortisone injections within 4 weeks of surgery
criteria.question: Has the individual had no intra-articular cortisone injection in the 4 weeks before the planned surgery (most recent injection at least 4 weeks before surgery)?

criteria.text: Symptom onset, duration, and severity
criteria.question: Do the clinical notes record when the symptoms began, how long they have lasted and how severe they are?

criteria.text: Loss of function and/or limitations
criteria.question: Do the clinical notes describe the loss of function and/or limitations?

criteria.text: Type and duration of non-operative management modalities (where applicable)
criteria.question: Do the clinical notes record the type and the duration of each non-operative management modality tried?

criteria.text: Rest or activity modifications/limitations
criteria.question: Was rest or activity modification/limitation tried?

criteria.text: Ice/heat
criteria.question: Was ice or heat therapy tried?

criteria.text: Protected weight bearing
criteria.question: Was protected weight bearing tried?

criteria.text: Pharmacologic treatment: oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics, tramadol
criteria.question: Was pharmacologic treatment (oral/topical NSAIDs, acetaminophen, analgesics or tramadol) tried?

criteria.text: Brace/orthosis
criteria.question: Was a brace or orthosis tried?

criteria.text: Physical therapy modalities
criteria.question: Were physical therapy modalities tried?

criteria.text: Supervised home exercise
criteria.question: Was a supervised home exercise program tried?

criteria.text: Weight optimization
criteria.question: Was weight optimization tried?

criteria.text: Corticosteroid injection
criteria.question: Was a corticosteroid injection tried?

criteria.text: Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment
criteria.question: Has at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment failed to relieve the symptoms?

criteria.text: Failure of at least 6 weeks of non-operative treatment
criteria.question: Has at least 6 weeks of non-operative treatment failed to relieve the symptoms?

criteria.text: Failure of at least 6 months of non-operative treatment
criteria.question: Has at least 6 months of non-operative treatment failed to relieve the symptoms?

criteria.text: At least 12 weeks of knee pain with documented loss of function
criteria.question: Has the individual had knee pain with documented loss of function for at least 12 weeks?

criteria.text: History of painful weight bearing
criteria.question: Is there a history of painful weight bearing?

criteria.text: physical examination that shows joint line tenderness, effusion and/or limited motion compared to pre-symptomatic joint range
criteria.question: Does the physical examination show joint line tenderness, effusion and/or limited motion compared with the pre-symptomatic range?

criteria.text: Indeterminate radiographs AND MRI findings
criteria.question: Are both the radiographs and the MRI findings indeterminate?

criteria.text: Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3-4 changes (based on weight-bearing radiographs)
criteria.question: Do weight-bearing radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3-4 changes?

criteria.text: meniscus tears
criteria.question: Does imaging show a meniscus tear?

criteria.text: ligament tears
criteria.question: Does imaging show a ligament tear?

criteria.text: loose bodies
criteria.question: Does imaging show loose bodies?

criteria.text: stress fractures (including insufficiency fractures)
criteria.question: Does imaging show a stress or insufficiency fracture?

criteria.text: patellofemoral instability (lateral patellar tilt or patellar subluxation)
criteria.question: Does imaging show patellofemoral instability (lateral patellar tilt or patellar subluxation)?

criteria.text: Two or more or persistent effusion(s)
criteria.question: Has the individual had two or more effusions, or a persistent effusion?

criteria.text: MRI results demonstrate evidence of an area of localized articular cartilage damage or an unstable chondral flap
criteria.question: Does the MRI show an area of localized articular cartilage damage or an unstable chondral flap?

criteria.text: Anterior knee pain with documented loss of function, exacerbated by activities that load the patellofemoral joint such as ascending or descending stairs or being in seated position for extended periods of time with knee flexed
criteria.question: Is there anterior knee pain with documented loss of function that is worsened by activities loading the patellofemoral joint (stairs, prolonged sitting with the knee flexed)?

criteria.text: excluded (referred hip pain, radicular pain, tendinitis, bursitis, neuroma)
criteria.question: Have other sources of pain or dysfunction (referred hip pain, radicular pain, tendinitis, bursitis, neuroma) been excluded?

criteria.text: Physical exam localizes tenderness to the patellofemoral joint
criteria.question: Does the physical exam localize tenderness to the patellofemoral joint?

criteria.text: No evidence of moderate to severe osteoarthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3-4 based on weight-bearing radiographs and patellofemoral views [see Grading Appendix])
criteria.question: Do weight-bearing radiographs with patellofemoral views show no moderate or severe osteoarthritis (no Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3-4)?

criteria.text: Symptomatic meniscal tear confirmed by MRI results that demonstrate a peripheral tear in the vascular zone, root tear, (10) or other tear that the requesting physician considers repairable
criteria.question: Does the MRI confirm a symptomatic meniscal tear that is a peripheral tear in the vascular zone, a root tear, or another tear the requesting physician considers repairable?

criteria.text: is associated with pain localized to the corresponding compartment upon physical examination
criteria.question: On physical examination, is the pain localized to the compartment of the meniscal tear?

criteria.text: No Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3-4 changes on standing X-rays
criteria.question: Do standing X-rays show no Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3-4 changes?

criteria.text: MRI demonstrate a meniscus tear in a patient age <21 years
criteria.question: Does the MRI show a meniscus tear in a patient younger than 21 years?

criteria.text: complains of pain or mechanical symptoms
criteria.question: Does the patient complain of pain or mechanical symptoms?

criteria.text: has ANY positive meniscal findings on physical examination
criteria.question: Does the physical examination show any positive meniscal finding?

criteria.text: MRI demonstrates a bucket-handle tear of the meniscus
criteria.question: Does the MRI show a bucket-handle tear of the meniscus?

criteria.text: there is a history of acute injury/onset of symptoms with a locked knee and/or mechanical symptoms of locking
criteria.question: Is there a history of acute injury or acute onset of symptoms with a locked knee and/or mechanical locking?

criteria.text: Knee joint line pain with forced hyperextension upon physical exam
criteria.question: Does forced hyperextension on exam produce joint line pain?

criteria.text: Knee joint line pain with maximum flexion upon physical exam
criteria.question: Does maximum flexion on exam produce joint line pain?

criteria.text: Knee pain, crepitus, or an audible or palpable click with the McMurray's test or Apley grind test
criteria.question: Does the McMurray's or Apley grind test produce pain, crepitus or an audible or palpable click?

criteria.text: Joint line tenderness to palpation upon physical exam
criteria.question: Is there joint line tenderness to palpation on exam?

criteria.text: history of mechanical symptoms such as 'catching' or 'locking'
criteria.question: Is there a history of mechanical symptoms such as catching or locking?

criteria.text: Weight-bearing X-rays (standing X-rays, Rosenberg view, 45-degree flexed PA view, etc.) demonstrate no moderate or severe osteoarthritic changes defined as Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3-4 [see Grading Appendix]; X-rays should be described as showing either no arthritis or mild/minimal arthritis only
criteria.question: Do weight-bearing X-rays show no moderate or severe osteoarthritis (no Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3-4), described as no arthritis or mild/minimal arthritis only?

criteria.text: MRI results confirm a frank meniscal tear (not simply degenerative changes, i.e., fraying)
criteria.question: Does the MRI confirm a frank meniscal tear rather than only degenerative change or fraying?

criteria.text: moderate or severe articular cartilage thinning
criteria.question: Does the MRI show moderate or severe articular cartilage thinning?

criteria.text: full-thickness articular cartilage loss or defects
criteria.question: Does the MRI show full-thickness articular cartilage loss or defects?

criteria.text: extrusion of the meniscus
criteria.question: Does the MRI show extrusion of the meniscus?

criteria.text: subchondral edema
criteria.question: Does the MRI show subchondral edema?

criteria.text: more than mild osteophytes
criteria.question: Does the MRI show more than mild osteophytes?

criteria.text: subchondral cysts
criteria.question: Does the MRI show subchondral cysts?

criteria.text: an impression of 'moderate' or 'advanced/severe' arthritis
criteria.question: Does the MRI report give an impression of moderate or advanced/severe arthritis?

criteria.text: Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4 osteoarthritis
criteria.question: Is Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 osteoarthritis present?

criteria.text: Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 osteoarthritis
criteria.question: Is Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 osteoarthritis present?

criteria.text: There has been the acute onset of locking (does not include catching, popping, cracking, etc.)
criteria.question: Has there been an acute onset of true locking (not catching, popping or cracking)?

criteria.text: There is MRI evidence of a bucket-handle or displaced meniscal fragment that correlates with the correct compartment (i.e., medial tenderness and locking, for a medial meniscus tear)
criteria.question: Does the MRI show a bucket-handle or displaced meniscal fragment in the compartment that matches the tenderness and locking?

criteria.text: Individual is < 40 years of age
criteria.question: Is the individual younger than 40?

criteria.text: Individual has no evidence of arthritic changes
criteria.question: Is there no evidence of arthritic changes in the knee?

criteria.text: Symptomatic meniscal deficiency confirmed by MRI results that show a meniscal deficient compartment
criteria.question: Does the MRI confirm a symptomatic meniscal-deficient compartment?

criteria.text: previous arthroscopy photographs or video showing subtotal or total meniscectomy
criteria.question: Do photographs or video from a previous arthroscopy show a subtotal or total meniscectomy?

criteria.text: Uncorrected (staged or simultaneous) ligamentous insufficiency (ACL, PCL, MCL, LCL, PMC, PLC)
criteria.question: Is there ligamentous insufficiency (ACL, PCL, MCL, LCL, PMC, PLC) that is not being corrected, staged or simultaneously?

criteria.text: Uncorrected (staged or simultaneous) malalignment greater than 5 degrees varus or 5 degrees valgus
criteria.question: Is there malalignment greater than 5 degrees varus or valgus that is not being corrected, staged or simultaneously?

criteria.text: Uncorrected (staged or simultaneous) full-thickness articular cartilage isolated defects (International Cartilage Research Society Grade 3 or 4; Outerbridge Grade IV [see Grading Appendix])
criteria.question: Is there an uncorrected full-thickness articular cartilage defect (ICRS grade 3 or 4, Outerbridge grade IV)?

criteria.text: Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4 osteoarthritis
criteria.question: Is Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or 4 osteoarthritis present?

criteria.text: individual has no evidence of severe arthritis defined as Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or 4
criteria.question: Is there no evidence of severe arthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or 4)? An MRI with no mention of significant arthritis suffices; if the MRI shows significant arthritis, standing X-rays must confirm no grade 3 or 4 changes.

criteria.text: Acute ACL tear confirmed by MRI
criteria.question: Does the MRI confirm an acute ACL tear?

criteria.text: Marx activity score for athletics (any score > 4)
criteria.question: Is a Marx activity score greater than 4 documented?

criteria.text: Tegner activity score for athletics and/or occupation ((score > 2)
criteria.question: Is a Tegner activity score greater than 2 documented for athletics and/or occupation?

criteria.text: MRI results confirm an ACL tear
criteria.question: Does the MRI confirm an ACL tear?

criteria.text: associated with other ligamentous instability or repairable meniscus
criteria.question: Is the ACL tear associated with other ligamentous instability or a repairable meniscus tear?

criteria.text: Patient history of instability at the time of an acute injury or history of recurrent knee instability (as defined subjectively as 'giving way', 'giving out', 'buckling', two-fist sign)
criteria.question: Is there a history of instability at the time of an acute injury, or of recurrent knee instability (giving way, giving out, buckling, two-fist sign)?

criteria.text: Physical examination findings demonstrate a positive Lachman test, Lachman test 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B, 3A, 3B, anterior drawer, pivot shift test, or instrumented (KT-1000 or KT-2000) laxity of greater than 3 mm side-side difference
criteria.question: Does the physical examination show a positive Lachman, anterior drawer or pivot shift test, or instrumented (KT-1000/KT-2000) laxity greater than 3 mm side-to-side difference?

criteria.text: MRI results confirm complete ACL tear or substantial partial tear with a non-functioning ACL as demonstrated on physical examination
criteria.question: Does the MRI confirm a complete ACL tear, or a substantial partial tear with an ACL shown to be non-functioning on exam?

criteria.text: Knee instability (as defined subjectively as 'giving way', 'giving out' or 'buckling')
criteria.question: Does the individual report knee instability (giving way, giving out or buckling)?

criteria.text: clinical findings of any of the following signs/tests: positive posterior drawer, posterior sag, quadriceps active, dial test at 90 degrees knee flexion or reverse pivot shift test
criteria.question: Is a positive posterior drawer, posterior sag, quadriceps active, dial test at 90 degrees or reverse pivot shift test documented?

criteria.text: MRI results confirm complete PCL tear
criteria.question: Does the MRI confirm a complete PCL tear?

criteria.text: Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment, including physical therapy emphasizing quadriceps strengthening
criteria.question: Has at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment, including physical therapy emphasizing quadriceps strengthening, failed?

criteria.text: Absence of medial and patellofemoral K-L grade 3-4 changes in chronic tears
criteria.question: For a chronic tear, are medial and patellofemoral Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3-4 changes absent?

criteria.text: chronic tears
criteria.question: Is the PCL tear chronic (rather than acute/subacute)?

criteria.text: All non-traumatic collateral ligament repair/reconstruction requests will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis
criteria.question: Collateral ligament repair/reconstruction is decided case-by-case by a reviewer; no chart criteria are given.

criteria.text: Skeletally immature patient
criteria.question: Is the patient skeletally immature (open growth plates)?

criteria.text: Individual is symptomatic (pain, swelling, mechanical symptoms of popping, locking, catching, or limited range of motion)
criteria.question: Is the individual symptomatic (pain, swelling, popping, locking, catching or limited range of motion)?

criteria.text: Asymptomatic patients will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis
criteria.question: Asymptomatic patients are decided case-by-case by a reviewer.

criteria.text: Radiographic findings (X-ray or MRI) of a displaced osteochondral lesion
criteria.question: Does X-ray or MRI show a displaced osteochondral lesion?

criteria.text: Radiographic findings (X-ray or MRI) findings of a stable osteochondral lesion
criteria.question: Does X-ray or MRI show a stable osteochondral lesion?

criteria.text: Exclude individuals with evidence of meniscal deficiency and/or malalignment if these are not being addressed (meniscal transplant and/or lateral release/patellar realignment procedure) at the same time as the cartilage restoration procedure
criteria.question: Does the individual have meniscal deficiency and/or malalignment that is NOT being addressed (meniscal transplant, lateral release/patellar realignment) at the same time as the cartilage procedure?

criteria.text: Skeletally mature adult
criteria.question: Is the individual a skeletally mature adult?

criteria.text: Individuals are symptomatic with anterior knee pain, swelling, mechanical symptoms of popping, locking, catching, or limited range of motion
criteria.question: Is the individual symptomatic with anterior knee pain, swelling, popping, locking, catching or limited range of motion?

criteria.text: physical examination findings should be localized to the patellofemoral joint
criteria.question: For a trochlear or patellar lesion, are the physical examination findings localized to the patellofemoral joint?

criteria.text: trochlea or patellar lesions
criteria.question: Is the lesion in the trochlea or patella?

criteria.text: MRI confirms an isolated full-thickness chondral or osteochondral lesion of the femoral condyle, trochlea, or patella < 2.0 cm2
criteria.question: Does the MRI confirm an isolated full-thickness chondral or osteochondral lesion of the femoral condyle, trochlea or patella smaller than 2.0 cm2?

criteria.text: Physical exam findings and/or (imaging) results confirm no ligamentous instability
criteria.question: Do the exam and/or imaging confirm there is no ligamentous instability?

criteria.text: femoral condyle lesions
criteria.question: Is the lesion in a femoral condyle?

criteria.text: no evidence of prior meniscectomy in same compartment
criteria.question: Is there no prior meniscectomy in the same compartment as the lesion?

criteria.text: concurrent meniscal transplant performed
criteria.question: Is a concurrent meniscal transplant being performed?

criteria.text: Individual has been symptomatic (pain, swelling, mechanical symptoms of popping, locking, catching, or limited range of motion) for at least 6 months
criteria.question: Has the individual been symptomatic (pain, swelling, popping, locking, catching or limited range of motion) for at least 6 months?

criteria.text: Individual is < 50 years of age
criteria.question: Is the individual younger than 50?

criteria.text: BMI < 35 (optimal outcomes if patient BMI < 30)
criteria.question: Is the BMI below 35?

criteria.text: No prior meniscectomy in same compartment
criteria.question: Has there been no prior meniscectomy in the same compartment?

criteria.text: concurrent or staged meniscal transplant performed
criteria.question: Is a concurrent or staged meniscal transplant being performed?

criteria.text: MRI results confirm an isolated full thickness chondral or osteochondral lesion of the femoral condyles or trochlea with stable surrounding articular cartilage
criteria.question: Does the MRI confirm an isolated full-thickness chondral or osteochondral lesion of the femoral condyle or trochlea with stable surrounding cartilage?

criteria.text: < 2.0 cm2 - OAT
criteria.question: Is the lesion smaller than 2.0 cm2 (the size for OAT)?

criteria.text: > 2.0 cm2 - ACI, MACI, OCA
criteria.question: Is the lesion larger than 2.0 cm2 (the size for ACI, MACI or OCA)?

criteria.text: MRI and/or physical findings confirm knee has normal alignment as defined as +/- 3 degrees from neutral on full-length mechanical axis long-leg x-ray
criteria.question: Do MRI and/or physical findings confirm normal alignment, within 3 degrees of neutral on a full-length mechanical-axis long-leg X-ray?

criteria.text: concurrent or staged tibial or femoral osteotomy performed
criteria.question: Is a concurrent or staged tibial or femoral osteotomy being performed?

criteria.text: stability
criteria.question: Is the knee ligamentously stable?

criteria.text: concurrent ligamentous repair or reconstruction performed
criteria.question: Is a concurrent ligamentous repair or reconstruction being performed?

criteria.text: MRI and/or X-rays shows no evidence of osteoarthritis
criteria.question: Do MRI and/or weight-bearing X-rays show no osteoarthritis beyond Kellgren-Lawrence grade 2?

criteria.text: Anterior knee pain and loss of function
criteria.question: Is there anterior knee pain with loss of function?

criteria.text: Other extra-articular or intra-articular sources of pain or dysfunction have been excluded (referred pain, radicular pain, tendinitis, bursitis, neuroma)
criteria.question: Have other sources of pain or dysfunction (referred pain, radicular pain, tendinitis, bursitis, neuroma) been excluded?

criteria.text: Physical exam localizes tenderness to the patellofemoral joint with pain aggravated by activities that load the joint (single leg squat, descending > ascending stairs or stair climbing, and being in seated position for extended periods of time with knee flexed)
criteria.question: Does the exam localize tenderness to the patellofemoral joint, with pain aggravated by loading activities (single-leg squat, stairs, prolonged sitting with the knee flexed)?

criteria.text: MRI results confirm an isolated full thickness chondral or osteochondral lesion of the patella
criteria.question: Does the MRI confirm an isolated full-thickness chondral or osteochondral lesion of the patella?

criteria.text: No evidence of associated osteoarthritis greater than Kellgren-Lawrence 2 of the patellofemoral joint or medial/lateral compartments on weight bearing X-rays
criteria.question: Do weight-bearing X-rays show no osteoarthritis beyond Kellgren-Lawrence grade 2 in the patellofemoral joint or the medial/lateral compartments?

criteria.text: document Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or 4 changes
criteria.question: Do patellofemoral X-rays document Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or 4 changes?

criteria.text: no more than K-L 2 changes of the medial and lateral compartments on weight-bearing X-rays
criteria.question: Do weight-bearing X-rays show no more than Kellgren-Lawrence grade 2 changes in the medial and lateral compartments?

criteria.text: Proliferative rheumatoid synovium (in individuals with established rheumatoid arthritis)
criteria.question: Is there proliferative rheumatoid synovium in an individual with established rheumatoid arthritis?

criteria.text: Non-responsive to disease modifying drug (DMARD) therapy for at least 6 months
criteria.question: Has the synovitis failed to respond to at least 6 months of DMARD therapy?

criteria.text: At least one instance of aspiration of joint effusion and corticosteroid injection (if no evidence of infection)
criteria.question: Has the joint effusion been aspirated and a corticosteroid injected at least once (absent infection)?

criteria.text: Hemarthrosis from injury, coagulopathy or bleeding disorder confirmed by physical exam, joint aspiration, and/or MRI
criteria.question: Is a hemarthrosis from injury, coagulopathy or a bleeding disorder confirmed by exam, aspiration and/or MRI?

criteria.text: Proliferative pigmented villonodular synovitis, synovial chondromatosis, sarcoid synovitis, or similar proliferative synovial disease, traumatic hypertrophic synovitis, cyclops lesion, or fat pad syndrome confirmed by history, MRI, or biopsy
criteria.question: Is PVNS, synovial chondromatosis, sarcoid or similar proliferative synovitis, traumatic hypertrophic synovitis, a cyclops lesion or fat pad syndrome confirmed by history, MRI or biopsy?

criteria.text: At least one instance of aspiration of joint effusion and injection of corticosteroid (if no evidence of infection)
criteria.question: Has the joint effusion been aspirated and a corticosteroid injected at least once (absent infection)?

criteria.text: Patient is symptomatic and there is detection of a painful plica confirmed by physical exam
criteria.question: Is the patient symptomatic with a painful plica detected on physical exam?

criteria.text: MRI confirms the presence of a plica
criteria.question: Does the MRI confirm a plica?

criteria.text: Documentation of mechanical symptoms that cause limitation or loss of function
criteria.question: Are mechanical symptoms causing limitation or loss of function documented?

criteria.text: X-ray, CT, or MRI documentation of a loose body
criteria.question: Does X-ray, CT or MRI document a loose body?

criteria.text: No evidence of patellar dislocation
criteria.question: Is there no evidence of patellar dislocation?

criteria.text: Reproducible isolated lateral patellofemoral pain with patellar tilt test
criteria.question: Does the patellar tilt test reproduce isolated lateral patellofemoral pain?

criteria.text: Evidence of lateral patellar tilt from radiologic images (patellofemoral view: Merchant (45 degrees flexion; and/or skyline (60-90 degrees flexion); and/or sunrise (60-90 degrees flexion)
criteria.question: Do patellofemoral-view images (Merchant, skyline or sunrise) show lateral patellar tilt?

criteria.text: Associated lateral patella facet Kellgren-Lawrence changes grade 1, 2, or 3
criteria.question: Does the lateral patellar facet show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1, 2 or 3 changes?

criteria.text: No evidence of medial patellofemoral changes (Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 2 osteoarthritis or higher [see Grading Appendix])
criteria.question: Is the medial patellofemoral compartment free of Kellgren-Lawrence grade 2 or higher changes?

criteria.text: quadriceps strengthening
criteria.question: Did the non-operative program include quadriceps strengthening?

criteria.text: appropriate hamstring/IT band stretching
criteria.question: Did the non-operative program include hamstring/IT band stretching?

criteria.text: patellar mobilization techniques
criteria.question: Did the non-operative program include patellar mobilization techniques?

criteria.text: Acute traumatic patellar dislocation is associated with an osteochondral fracture, loose body, vastus medialis obliquus/medial patellofemoral ligament muscle avulsion, or other intra-articular injury that requires urgent operative management
criteria.question: Is an acute traumatic patellar dislocation associated with an osteochondral fracture, loose body, VMO/MPFL avulsion or other intra-articular injury requiring urgent operative management?

criteria.text: First time patellar dislocation (not subluxation)
criteria.question: Is this a first-time patellar dislocation (not a subluxation)?

criteria.text: Age < 25
criteria.question: Is the individual younger than 25?

criteria.text: TT-TG distance of 15 mm or greater
criteria.question: Does imaging show a tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance of 15 mm or greater?

criteria.text: Trochlear dysplasia
criteria.question: Does imaging show trochlear dysplasia?

criteria.text: Patella alta
criteria.question: Does imaging show patella alta?

criteria.text: History of 2 or more patellar dislocations
criteria.question: Is there a history of two or more patellar dislocations?

criteria.text: Radiologic confirmation of MPFL (medial patellofemoral ligament) deficiency (including evidence of acute or remote injury, scarring, incomplete healing, etc.)
criteria.question: Does imaging confirm MPFL deficiency (acute or remote injury, scarring, incomplete healing)?

criteria.text: Physical examination demonstrates evidence of patellar instability (positive apprehension test, increased lateral patellar translation, etc.)
criteria.question: Does the physical examination show patellar instability (positive apprehension test, increased lateral translation)?

criteria.text: Patient complains of patellar subluxation or has a history of only one patellar dislocation
criteria.question: Does the patient complain of patellar subluxation, or have a history of only one dislocation?

criteria.text: Physical exam has patellofemoral tenderness and abnormal articulation of the patella in the femoral trochlear groove (patellar apprehension or positive J sign)
criteria.question: Does the exam show patellofemoral tenderness and abnormal patellar tracking (apprehension or positive J sign)?

criteria.text: Radiologic and/or advanced images (CT or MRI) rule out fracture or loose body
criteria.question: Do radiographs and/or CT or MRI rule out a fracture or loose body?

criteria.text: show abnormal articulation, trochlear dysplasia, abnormal TT-TG distance (tibial tubercle-trochlear groove) * or other abnormality related to malalignment
criteria.question: Does imaging show abnormal articulation, trochlear dysplasia, an abnormal TT-TG distance or another malalignment abnormality?

criteria.text: at least 3 months of physical therapy
criteria.question: Did the non-operative treatment include at least 3 months of physical therapy?

criteria.text: Individual is less than 20 weeks after ligamentous or joint reconstruction
criteria.question: Is the individual less than 20 weeks out from a ligamentous or joint reconstruction?

criteria.text: Physical exam findings demonstrate inadequate range of motion of the knee defined as less than 110 degrees of flexion or lack of full extension
criteria.question: Does the exam show flexion under 110 degrees or a lack of full extension?

criteria.text: Failure to improve range of motion of the knee despite 6 weeks (12 visits) of documented physical therapy
criteria.question: Has range of motion failed to improve despite 6 weeks (12 visits) of documented physical therapy?

criteria.text: Individual is > 12 weeks post-surgery fracture or resolved infection
criteria.question: Is the individual more than 12 weeks past the surgery, fracture or resolved infection?

criteria.text: Physical exam findings demonstrate inadequate range of motion of the knee, defined as < 110 degrees of flexion or lack of full extension
criteria.question: Does the exam show flexion under 110 degrees or a lack of full extension?

including at least two of the following

notes: The redline copy of the guideline still shows two deleted bullets, 'Individual has native knee' and 'Manipulation under anesthesia is also performed'; the clean copies and the November 2024 policy history ('Deleted the requirement for a manipulation under anesthesia when lysis of adhesion surgery is performed') drop them, so they are left out.

Source PDF holds three copies of the guideline: a redline with tracked changes merged into the text (29 pages, 'December 2023November 2024', 'July 20242025'), a clean 27-page copy and a clean 28-page copy that adds the Washington 20240920A section. The tree is built from the final clean 28-page copy (Last Revised November 2024, Implementation July 2025); redline-only text ('pediatric or adolescent individual', 'according to the American College of Rheumatology Guidelines', the two deleted lysis bullets) is not used.

Payer: 'Evolent' refers to Evolent Health LLC and Evolent Specialty Services, Inc. Lines of business checked: CHIP, Commercial, Exchange/Marketplace, Medicaid; Medicare Advantage is unchecked and is recorded under excluded_plans.

General requirements ('Elective arthroscopic surgery of the knee may be considered if the following general criteria are met') are placed inside every pathway's all(), including MUA, lysis of adhesions and the open codes, because the Purpose lists all of these among the procedures the guideline addresses.

The general bullet 'Individual is medically stable and optimized for surgery, and any treatable comorbidities are adequately medically managed ...' holds two requirements and is split in two; the following sentence on shared decision applies only 'when comorbidities exist' and is modelled as any(shared decision, not(comorbidities exist)).

Modelling convention for conditional requirements ('when comorbidities exist', 'For trochlea or patellar lesions', 'For femoral condyle lesions', 'in chronic tears'): any(requirement, not(condition)), with the condition as its own criterion so a chart without the condition is not asked for the requirement.
'Individual does not have active, untreated drug dependency ... unless engaged in a treatment program' is any(no untreated dependency, engaged in a treatment program).

'Clinical notes should address' symptom onset/duration/severity and loss of function/limitations are included in the general block as documentation criteria. 'Type and duration of non-operative management modalities (where applicable)' is placed beside each non-operative trial requirement and omitted from pathways that require no trial (ACL, collateral, loose body removal, meniscectomy Sections One-Three, synovectomy Section Two, cartilage immature Section One, patellar instability Sections One-Three).

The general rule 'Unless otherwise stated in the subsections below, non-operative management must include at least TWO or more of the following' (whose list ends 'Injections: corticosteroid, NSAID, viscosupplementation') is superseded in every subsection that requires a trial by that subsection's own list (ending 'Corticosteroid injection') and count, so the general list is not a separate set of criteria. It is read as governing the content of a trial where one is required, not as imposing a trial on pathways that list none (loose body removal, ACL, meniscectomy Sections One-Three, etc.).
'At least two of the following' modality lists are expanded as any of the pairs (9 modalities = 36 pairs); 'at least one of the following' is a plain any.

Durations are converted at 4 weeks = 1 month: 12 weeks = 3 months, 6 weeks = 1.5, 4 weeks = 1, 20 weeks = 5. 'No intra-articular cortisone injections within 4 weeks of surgery' is typed as at least 1 month between the last injection and surgery.

'No intra-articular cortisone injections within 4 weeks of surgery' is repeated at the end of most subsections and as an absolute contraindication; it is one criterion in the general block, not repeated per pathway.

Negatively phrased bullets that the document lists as criteria ('No evidence of ...', 'No Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3-4 changes on standing X-rays', 'Individual does not have ...') are kept as leaves with the bullet text. 'Should not demonstrate any of the following', 'does not demonstrate any of the following', 'Absolute Contraindications' and 'Exclude individuals with ...' are not(any(...)).
Kellgren-Lawrence grades are typed as numbers 0-4 (unit 'Kellgren-Lawrence grade'): 'no grade 3-4' = lte 2; 'grade 3 or 4' = gte 3.

Code assignment: the document groups codes only under four headings (MUA; Ligament Reconstruction/Repair; Meniscectomy/Meniscal Repair/Meniscal Transplant; Knee Surgery - Other). Within a heading, codes are assigned to pathways by their standard CPT descriptors (29870 diagnostic; 29877/G0289 chondroplasty; 29880/29881 and 27332/27333 meniscectomy; 29882/29883/27403 meniscal repair; 29868 transplant; 29888 ACL; 29889 PCL; open ligament codes 27405-27429 to all three ligament pathways; 29879 and 29885-29887 marrow stimulation/drilling; 29866/27416 OAT; 29867/27415 OCA; 27412 ACI; 29874/G0289 loose body; 29875/29876 synovectomy; 29873/27425 lateral release; 27418-27424 patellar realignment/tibial tubercle; 27570 MUA; 29884 lysis and MUA). A reviewer using only the document's headings would spread each heading's codes over all its pathways.

Every code in the table is tagged covered: the document says nothing adverse about any code. Abrasion arthroplasty 'is not indicated' but 29879 also describes microfracture and multiple drilling, so 29879 stays covered and the note is an exclusion without codes.

The Washington legislative language (HTCC 20080815B: arthroscopy for osteoarthritis not a covered benefit; HTCC 20240920A: MACI/ACI, OATS and OCA covered with conditions - symptomatic full-thickness Outerbridge III/IV defects, closed growth plates, age < 50, BMI < 35, no malignancy/KL 3-4/inflammatory arthritis, MACI >= 3 cm2, OATS 2-4 cm2; cell-free implants and AMIC not covered; uncorrected malalignment or ligamentous deficiency non-covered unless corrected) applies to Washington members only. The not-covered statements are recorded as exclusions; the HTCC conditions are not built as a pathway because the fixture has no state gate and a state-only pathway would govern every chart.
'Subchondroplasty and In-office diagnostic arthroscopy (e.g., Mi-Eye, VisionScope) are not managed by Evolent' is an out-of-scope note, not an exclusion.
Statement/General Information ('care/services from a licensed clinician'; supporting documentation 'must be provided') are submission expectations, not clinical criteria, and are left out.
The Background section's statement that only one of MRI or X-rays is required for meniscectomy approval is reflected in the Section Four any(X-ray, MRI) node.

The Articular Cartilage Restoration and Repair Exclusions list ('excluded from consideration under this guideline') is recorded as one exclusion; the June 2023 history calls it the 'Listing of investigational/non-covered articular cartilage procedures'. No code in the table describes only those products, so cpt is empty.

Meniscectomy Section One's single bullet holds a tear requirement and an exam requirement and is split in two; the MRI tear leaf keeps the citation marker '(10)' because it is inside the verbatim span.

Meniscectomy Section Two ('MRI demonstrate a meniscus tear in a patient age <21 years who complains of pain or mechanical symptoms or has ANY positive meniscal findings on physical examination') is all(MRI tear and age < 21, any(pain or mechanical symptoms, positive meniscal exam)).
Grading Appendix tables (Kellgren-Lawrence, Outerbridge, Marx, Tegner) are definitions, not criteria.

Descriptive sentences left out as guidance, not requirements: 'The OAT or OCA procedures are preferable if the lesion involves subchondral bone'; 'Collateral ligament repair or reconstruction should rarely occur independent of additional ligament repair or reconstruction surgery'; the Lateral Release/Patellar Realignment and Lysis of Adhesions introductions; 'Diagnostic knee arthroscopy should rarely be required'; the Scope sentence on open non-arthroplasty surgery.

Three criterion texts are shortened to the part of the sentence on one side of a page break or a hyphenated line break, because the verbatim check keeps the running page header between the halves: patellofemoral chondroplasty 'Other extra-articular or intra-articular sources of pain or dysfunction have been | excluded (referred hip pain, ...)' keeps the second half; restorative femoral condyle 'MRI and/or X-rays shows no evidence of osteoarthritis (no greater than Kellgren-|Lawrence Grade 2 changes on weight-bearing X-rays)' keeps the first half with the KL <= 2 threshold typed from the parenthetical; patellofemoral chondrosis 'patellofemoral X-rays should | document Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or 4 changes' keeps the second half.

exclusions.text: Arthroscopic meniscectomy or meniscal repair is never medically necessary in the presence of Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4 osteoarthritis
ANY intra-articular cortisone injections within 4 weeks of surgery
Meniscectomy or repair is considered NOT MEDICALLY NECESSARY in the presence of Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 osteoarthritis
If grade 3 changes are present, only a meniscectomy may be indicated, not a repair.
If there is evidence of meniscal extrusion on coronal MRI, with/without subchondral edema, arthroscopy is relatively contraindicated, even if a tear is present

Absolute Contraindications: Meniscal Transplant (11) Uncorrected (staged or simultaneous) ligamentous insufficiency (ACL, PCL, MCL, LCL, PMC, PLC) Uncorrected (staged or simultaneous) malalignment greater than 5 degrees varus or 5 degrees valgus Uncorrected (staged or simultaneous) full-thickness articular cartilage isolated defects (International Cartilage Research Society Grade 3 or 4; Outerbridge Grade IV [see Grading Appendix]) Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4 osteoarthritis [see Grading Appendix]

Exclude individuals with evidence of meniscal deficiency and/or malalignment if these are not being addressed (meniscal transplant and/or lateral release/patellar realignment procedure) at the same time as the cartilage restoration procedure
NOTE: Abrasion arthroplasty is included in coding but is not indicated

These requests are excluded from consideration under this guideline: Micronized cartilage extracellular matrix (BioCartilage) Autologous Matrix-Induced Chondrogenesis (AMIC) Bone marrow aspirate concentrate (BMAC) implantation Hybrid ACI/OAT procedure Particulated juvenile allograft cartilage (PJAC, DeNovo) Particulated autologous cartilage implantation (PACI) Viable cartilage allograft putty (CartiMax) Decellularized Osteochondral Allograft Plugs (e.g., Chondrofix) Cryopreserved viable osteochondral allograft (CVOCA; Cartiform and ProChondrix) Aragonite biphasic osteochondral scaffolds (Agili-C™) Human umbilical cord blood-derived mesenchymal stem cells (CARTISEM)
Knee Arthroscopy for osteoarthritis of the knee is not a covered benefit. This decision does not apply to the use of knee arthroscopy for other diagnostic and therapeutic purposes.
Treatments for chondral defects of the knee with cell-free implants and autologous matrix-induced chondrogenesis (AMIC) are not covered benefits.
Uncorrected malalignment or ligamentous deficiency, unless a corrective procedure is performed prior to or concomitantly.
